- When sentiment is bullish (≥0.5) and model forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope if supply net is negative or event count is high — avoid over-optimism.  
- If true outcome spikes sharply after a low, model often underreacts — adjust forecast to include a slight lagged overshoot correction.  
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d) with negative supply net, model tends to over-predict recovery — cap forecast growth at 1–2% per day after peak.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.3) and model is flat, model underestimates downside — add 0.5–1.0% downward bias to forecast if supply net is negative.  
- If sentiment history shows recent bullish spikes followed by bearish reversal, model often fails to revert — apply mean reversion to forecast 3–5 days after peak.  
- In low-event periods (≤10 events/30d), model tends to over-predict mean — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment is neutral or weak.  
- For auctions with supply net >0, model often overestimates price rise — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% if sentiment is neutral or weak.  
- If model forecast is rising but true outcome is flat or falling, reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day — avoid “over-leveraged” optimism.
